'''G. Bard Ermentrout''' is an American mathematician and distinguished professor at [[University of Pittsburgh]] and a member of the Odor2Action research network.<ref name="Mackenzie"/>  He uses
nonlinear dynamics for the mathematical modeling of problems in [[neuroscience]]. He explores patterns of activation in neural systems as they relate to biological problems such as [[olfaction]].<ref>{{cite web |title=G. Bard Ermentrout {{!}} Department of Mathematics |url=https://www.mathematics.pitt.edu/people/g-bard-ermentrout |website=University of Pittsburgh |access-date=14 March 2023}}</ref>

Bard Ermentrout is known for his contributions to computational and mathematical neuroscience. His joint work with Nancy Kopell derived the [[theta model|Ermentrout and Kopell canonical model]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ermentrout |first1=Bard |last2=Kopell |first2=Nancy |date=1984 |title=Frequency plateaus in a chain of weakly coupled oscillators, i. |journal=SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis |volume=15 |issue= 2|pages=215–237 |doi=10.1137/0515019 }}</ref> 
He and David Terman wrote the book ''Mathematical Foundations of Neuroscience''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ermentrout |first1=Bard |last2=Terman |first2=David |date=2010 |title=Mathematical Foundations of Neuroscience |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0-387-87708-2}}</ref> He helped to develop the dynamical systems software XPPAuto.<ref>{{cite book |last=Ermentrout |first=Bard |date=2002 |title=Simulating, analyzing, and animating dynamical systems: a guide to XPPAUT for researchers and students |publisher=SIAM |isbn=978-0-89871-506-4}}</ref>

One approach he uses in the study of olfaction is to program a virtual creature, implement various movement strategies for tracking scents, and examine their success rate under a different conditions. This enables researchers to better understand olfactory navigation strategies such as [[tropotaxis]] and [[klinotaxis]] and how they work in conditions such as high turbulence.<ref name="Mackenzie">{{cite journal |last1=Mackenzie |first1=Dana |title=How animals follow their nose |journal=Knowable Magazine |publisher=Annual Reviews |date=6 March 2023 |doi=10.1146/knowable-030623-4 |doi-access=free |url=https://knowablemagazine.org/article/living-world/2023/how-animals-follow-their-nose |access-date=13 March 2023 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Hengenius">{{cite journal |last1=Hengenius |first1=James B. |last2=Connor |first2=Erin G. |last3=Crimaldi |first3=John P. |last4=Urban |first4=Nathaniel N. |last5=Ermentrout |first5=G. Bard |title=Olfactory navigation in the real world: Simple local search strategies for turbulent environments |journal=Journal of Theoretical Biology |date=7 May 2021 |volume=516 |article-number=110607 |doi=10.1016/j.jtbi.2021.110607 |pmid=33524405 |s2cid=231755424 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022519321000291 |language=en |issn=0022-5193|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Outside of work, he is fond of his many pets and has owned many pet parrots over the years. He most recently owns a galah and two corgis. He is also a lover of limericks.
